description: Three independent guards. (1) Commit guard (commit-guard.sh, PreToolUse). Claude Code permissions.ask rules, installed by setup, prompt the human for every foreground git commit, git push, and pull request merge. The guard refuses a sub-agent's commit or push, a merge by a sub-agent or by the pipeline, a push that forces or deletes, and any of them behind bash -c, sh -c, env, eval, a leading NAME=value, or a program path, which the ask rules cannot see. It catches mistakes and is not a security boundary. (2) Pipeline scope (pipeline-scope.sh, PermissionRequest). For the scheduled pipeline only, marked by WORKBENCH_DEV_TEAM_PIPELINE=1 on the process bin/dispatch-agent.sh spawns, it allows a prompt for one plain git -C <dir>, rm, or rmdir command when every path is absolute and stays inside the roots: all of $TMPDIR, where every mktemp -d folder lands, so another run's clone is in scope too, and the scratch roots. The git subcommand must be add, checkout, commit, diff, log, merge, or push. It never allows a pull request merge, a force push, a push to the default branch, or a command a user deny rule matches. (3) Review guard (local-review-guard.sh, PreToolUse on Bash, Edit, Write, and NotebookEdit) — a static rule with no state: a call whose agent_type is Holmes, one of his mode agents (holmes-local, holmes-index), or his helper, holmes-lens, may not write outside the scratch roots ($TMPDIR, ~/Developer/scratchpad, and the session scratchpad). Reads and test runs stay legal, and every other agent is untouched. Each guard owns its own matcher blocks; none reads another's state. The hooks module (register.ts) is separate: it routes a dispatch of a dev-team agent to its mode agent, sets its model and effort from the config, and refuses a main-session brief that lacks a slot.
